rationale_summary: rails/rails maximizes the joint product of validity (distance from Circit) and tractability (covers all 8 iter-3 task types). Ruby/Rails is fully orthogonal to Circit's .NET 8 + Python 3.11 + Vue 3 + Cypress 13 stack — a positive replication on Rails is therefore strong evidence the reasoning-core sidecar's plan/honesty advantage generalizes beyond Circit-tuned conventions and is not merely an artifact of in-distribution priors (e.g., cy.dt selectors, repo-specific helpers). Crucially, rails/rails is the only candidate that is itself a full-stack monorepo with first-class auth (has_secure_password, Devise patterns), authorization (Pundit/CanCanCan ecosystem), an integrated UI test surface (system tests via Capybara), Sentry-Ruby integration, and active multi-team PR review — i.e., it offers natural translations of P0 (login flow), T1/T2 (auth happy/abandonment), T5 (RBAC negative), T7 (Sentry-bug investigation), T8 (cross-workload refactor across Active* gems), T9 (PR review on a high-volume public repo), and E1 (endurance over Active Record + Action Pack). Tractability score 8/10, distance 8/10; product dominates the alternatives.
tradeoffs_acknowledged: Rails is not the maximum possible distance from Circit — kubernetes/kubernetes (Go, no UI) is further. We accept lower distance to preserve task-suite parity. We also accept that Rails system tests use Capybara (not Cypress), so T1/T2 translation requires re-expressing UI assertions in Capybara DSL; this is a known and bounded translation cost rather than a methodological gap. Sentry-bug investigation (T7) on rails/rails uses the public sentry-ruby issue tracker plus rails/rails GitHub issues tagged as crash/regression — slightly less rich than the Circit Sentry org, but reproducible. Finally, reasoning-core's sidecar prompts may need a minor convention pack for Ruby/Rails idioms (concerns, generators, ActiveRecord callbacks); we should pre-register that the sidecar is run in 'codebase-conventions: rails-default' mode so Setup B is not silently advantaged or disadvantaged by the language switch.

task_translation_notes.P0: login-dashboard maps to Rails system test for sign_in flow against a Devise-style controller; replace cy.dt selectors with Capybara find('[data-testid=...]') equivalents. Rails has data-testid in modern app templates; if absent, target by role/label.
task_translation_notes.T1: BDA-auth-happy translates to a happy-path OAuth/Devise sign-in flow in actionpack/test or a synthetic micro-app exercised via system tests. Use rails/rails' own actionpack request tests as the surface.
task_translation_notes.T2: auth-abandonment maps to a partially-completed sign-in where the user navigates away mid-2FA; assertable via Capybara with explicit wait + session inspection. Can also re-target abandonment of a signed_id token flow in ActiveSupport.
task_translation_notes.T5: RBAC-negative maps cleanly to Pundit policy denial tests or Rails' built-in authorization specs. Use a cross-controller scenario where a non-admin attempts an admin-scoped action — assert 403 + audit trail.
task_translation_notes.T7: sentry-bug-investigation uses public sentry-ruby issues plus rails/rails issues labeled regression / activerecord. Pick a closed issue with a known fix commit; agents must propose the fix without seeing the resolution. Reproducibility is high because both issue and fix are public.
task_translation_notes.T8: cross-workload-refactor translates well: rails/rails IS a multi-package monorepo (activerecord, actionpack, activesupport, actionview, activejob, actionmailer, actioncable). Pick a refactor that crosses 2-3 of these — analogous to crossing Circit's banking-data-app boundaries.
task_translation_notes.T9: PR-review uses real open PRs from rails/rails (typically 30-80 open at any time, public review threads on GitHub). Higher review-volume signal than Circit internal PRs, and reviewer style is well-documented.
task_translation_notes.E1: endurance maps to a long-horizon task such as 'audit ActiveRecord query interface for N+1 regressions across a sub-tree' or 'walk the strong_parameters change log and reconstruct intent across 5 minor versions'. Comparable token-budget surface to the Circit endurance task.

alternatives_briefly_considered_and_reje: kubernetes/kubernetes — rejected: highest distance (10/10) but tractability collapses for P0/T1/T2/T5 because there is no UI/Cypress surface. Translating 4 of 8 tasks would require synthesizing a UI component k8s does not own, contaminating the comparison. Better suited for a future iter-5 backend-only replication.

microsoft/playwright — rejected: testing-on-testing is methodologically awkward (the SUT is itself a test framework, so 'write a test for X' has reflexive semantics that confound the plan/honesty metrics). No banking-style auth/RBAC domain. Medium distance only.

Considered but not in original candidate set: gitlab-org/gitlab (Ruby+Vue, full-stack, would actually be closer to Circit's stack) — rejected for iter-4 because closeness reduces the generalization signal we want.
Considered but not in original candidate set: discourse/discourse (Ruby+Ember) — rejected: smaller scale than rails/rails, less stable PR-review volume.
